subject: Privacy escalation: DPA notification routing, subprocessor cooperation and evidence export
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cardinalhealth.com, dpo@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: DPA incident notification routing + subprocessor asks

Team / Cardinal,

Quick summary: Cardinal asked for a hard 48-hour incident notification window in the DPA (for any incident impacting Personal Data), plus explicit subprocessor cooperation for forensic exports and vendor access. I returned their redline (attached) and asked for internal alignment before we re-engage.

Attachments: DPA_redline_v3.pdf, POC_roster.csv (stub)

Specific questions for us:
- Can we accept a fixed 48h for all incidents? (my initial read: too aggressive legally/operationally; risks overpromising when investigation ongoing)
- What is our stance on cross-border evidence export for forensics? Cardinal wants the right to request a forensic snapshot sent to their vendor in EU/US; we have export controls & subproc contractual constraints to consider.
- For subprocessor cooperation: do we require a written, scoped request + reimbursed vendor access, or do we allow unilateral access by the customer/conducting vendor?

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal propose compromise language for notification windows and attach a short compromise clause (48v72_compromise_clause.docx).
2) Kimberly: please draft a limited subprocessor cooperation appendix that requires scoped requests, lawful basis confirmation, and narrow data slices.
3) Grace: confirm acceptable forensic access controls (audit logs, limited retention, redaction rules).

Cardinal contacts copied so they have full visibility while we align. I want to have language back to them by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Note: attachment stubs only (we shared redline and the POC roster).

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA incident notification routing + subprocessor asks

Marcus —

High level reaction and recommended carve-outs:
- We should not agree to a universal 48-hour hardline. Regulated PII (PCI/PHI) is different from lower-risk PD. Suggest: 48 hours for confirmed compromise of regulated PII; 72 hours for other confirmed personal-data incidents; 7 days for "suspected" incidents while we triage. That gives us breathing room while meeting customer needs. (See attached compromise doc.)
- Forensics/export: we can permit export to Cardinal's named forensics vendor only after: (a) written request describing scope, (b) a legal basis check, (c) execution of a narrow access addendum with limited retention and audit obligations. We should avoid unfettered exports or jury-rigged neighbor accesses.
- Subprocessor cooperation: require written requests and a list of data elements to be shared; require Cardinal to route requests via Security Liaison (we'll provide a POC). We should also include reimbursement language for heavy forensic pulls.
- Operational ask: we need to map the escalation routing matrix into the DPA (who we notify internally and externally at what threshold). I've added a short POC roster and escalation flow in POC_roster.csv (stub).

If Cardinal insists on 48h across the board we should: (a) seek an SLA carveout for active investigation where notification can be updated, or (b) negotiate a penalty cap tied to confirmed regulatory harm.

I can draft the subproc appendix tonight and circulate.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

On attachments: 48v72_compromise_clause.docx attached (proposal).

From: security@cardinalhealth.com <security@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: dpo@cardinalhealth.com, legal@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:42:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Initial: DPA incident notification routing + subprocessor asks

Marcus / Kim / Grace,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the redline. Cardinal's position: 48 hours is a baseline we cannot move from for incidents affecting regulated PII (PHI/financial identifiers). Our rationale: regulatory timelines in our operating jurisdictions and our internal breach-response commitments to customers.

That said, we are prepared to accept a split-window approach on the DPA as you suggested: 48h for confirmed regulated PII, 72h for other confirmed personal data incidents. We need clarity on two operational points:
1) Detection vs confirmation: we consider the 48h clock to start from "confirmed unauthorized access" — not merely suspicion. Please ensure the clause is explicit.
2) Evidence export: Cardinal requires the ability to request a forensics snapshot routed to our approved vendor (we will supply vendor POA); however, export to a third country requires a documented lawful basis and a documented minimization step. We are fine with an addendum that includes documented scope + limited retention.

We will send a DocuSign link for the updated DPA once we have a short joint paragraph drafted. Please note our legal team will require the POC roster and the subprocessor appendix as part of the final sign-off.

Regards,
Cardinal Security Team
security@cardinalhealth.com

---
Attachment requests: please provide the POC roster and the proposed subprocessor appendix by COB Thursday. DocuSign link to follow: https://docusign.com/XYZ-Cardinal-DPA-001

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: security@cardinalhealth.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA incident notification routing + subprocessor asks

Thanks all — good progress. Summary / agreed internal plan: 

- Notification windows: propose hybrid language to Cardinal: 
  * 48 hours from "confirmation of unauthorized access" for regulated PII (PHI/financial identifiers),
  * 72 hours from confirmation for other personal data,
  * For "suspected" incidents we will notify within 7 days and update when confirmed.
- Detection vs confirmation: we'll add a definition section that clarifies when the clock begins ("confirmation" requires reasonable evidence of unauthorized access to a data set, not simply an alert).
- Evidence export & subprocessor cooperation: Kimberly to draft subprocessor cooperation appendix that requires: written scoped requests, lawful-basis attestation by Cardinal, named vendor list, limited retention, and an audit trail; Cardinal will reimburse extraordinary export costs.
- POC roster / routing matrix: Grace to finalize the internal notification ladder (Security -> Privacy -> Legal -> Ops) and supply the POC CSV for Cardinal.

Action owners & next steps: 
- Kimberly: circulate subprocessor_appendix_draft.docx by EOD Friday.
- Grace: finalize POC_roster.csv and escalation mapping by Friday noon.
- Marcus: send the joint paragraph (hybrid language) to Cardinal and await DocuSign then iterate.

I'll draft the paragraph and post to the Drive (link above) so Legal can redline. If Cardinal sends the DocuSign in the meantime, we will hold and propose the joint paragraph as an amendment.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
